When t<5 min: Figure 3(a) shows that the demand response request is false; and Figure 3(b) and Figure 3(d) show that the entire load is supported by the grid, and the BESS power output is zero. The SOC in Figure 3(c) is constant at the target SOC of 80%(using Algorithm 1). When 5<t<35 min: In Figure 3(a), the utility demand response request for 35 MW of BESS active power dispatch is received around t =5 min, and the PFMS responds to this request (using Algorithm 2). The BESS total output increases to 35 MW within 5 s (see Figure 4 for a zoomed-in view around the t =5- min or 300-s time window), and the power drawn from the grid decreases accordingly, as shown in Figure 3(b). In this time frame, the average SOC of the BESS units is decreasing linearly in Figure 3(c) due to the constant power output from the BESS units. Although the power drawn from the grid decreases substantially, the total IT and cooling loads do not experience any interruption, as no effect is observed on the load profiles in Figure 3(d). The PFMS helped reduce the effective data center load on the grid to cater to the utility’s request during the peak demand hours and thus improved the grid resilience. When t>35 min: The utility demand response ends, as shown in Figure 3(a). The PFMS starts to charge the BESS to the target the SOC (Algorithm 2) with 15 MW of charging power, which explains the neg- ative BESS output power curve shown in Figure 3(b). The charging of the BESS can also be verified by the increasing SOC in Figure 3(c) for t>35 min. The total IT and cooling load, along with the additional load due to charging the BESS, is supported by power from the grid. Accordingly, the power drawn from the grid increases compared to the grid power drawn for t <5 min. First, the PFMS uses the BESS units to provide backup power, and then, as the energy stored in the BESS units depletes and they reach below the low SOC threshold, it makes use of the generators. Once the power provided by the grid is stable, the PFMS will reconnect the system to the grid and initiate charging of the BESS units.
